beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output. You need a check.
beats.got: Looking at what an agent produces doesn't show whether it is safe, so you need a separate check.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: **Apply** named agent risk patterns (direct and indirect prompt injection, secrets in context, tool confusion, skill supply chain) and a plain access review
beats.got: A list of jargon. I don't know what it costs or who has to do it.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: I'm supposed to name my own checks. Fine, but I have no agent yet.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent turns its own text into actions. That is where the risk comes from. A long way to get there.

beats.trigger: You built something that works. Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: Nobody can promise certainty here, so the question is who signs for what.

beats.trigger: Classical software security is a risk-based practice, and the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: Old controls assumed predictable software, and agents aren't predictable.

beats.trigger: Together, you get *safe enough, under these conditions, within these limits, for now.*
beats.got: Safety is a conditional statement with limits and an expiry. I can put that in a board paper.

beats.trigger: Pick one risk and apply the smallest change that reduces it.
beats.got: Assess, then fix the smallest thing. It's a risk register routine with five named fixes. No cost or owner given.

beats.trigger: **Decide.** Accept the residual on record, or close the door.
beats.got: Residual risk is written down and someone formally accepts it. That is how I already run risk.

beats.trigger: Scope it down far enough and the system is safe and useless.
beats.got: Less access means less value, and someone has to choose where to stop and sign for it.

beats.trigger: Expect it to cost you a feature.
beats.got: The cheapest control is not connecting a system. I'd want the feature cost put as a number next to it.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: Nothing new. It repeats the loop and adds a mood line.

beats.trigger: A **skill** packages an expertise (rules, checklists, the moves an agent runs) into something the agent loads when the work matches.
beats.got: A skill is a reusable checklist the agent loads, so we keep it and don't re-explain each time.

beats.trigger: Read the first few rows: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: The agent scored our policy files rule by rule and some rows need a human.

beats.trigger: the customer your CEO would not want named in a transcript
beats.got: I tell it what matters to us in plain lines, so it's my own material. It also asks me to push back on generic output, which I will.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: Twenty-two minutes of Q&A. No time check against value.

beats.trigger: Answer what you can briefly, then hand back the rest: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: I can delegate the rest to the agent, and I still check that all four risk patterns are covered.

beats.trigger: The skill loads in your next session in this training directory.
beats.got: Install steps, which are IT's domain. Who approves a personal skill touching finance data?

beats.trigger: The reusable check carries the judgment about what matters in this system
beats.got: The value is our judgment written into a check, and it isn't the tool. A licence alone won't get us that.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: The aim is a documented process, not a pass.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The audit found things I hadn't thought of and marked some of my 'settled' items as unknown. That is useful.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: Ranked risk report, and I'm told to pick one. A feeling is not evidence.

beats.trigger: The risk remains. That is expected. Name it, accept it on record, and stop there.
beats.got: One risk is mitigated, the residual is written down and accepted. That is a record I can show.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report. Walk in with that.
beats.got: When the report can't settle it, I take the specific question to legal or IT with the evidence.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent.
beats.got: We did one risk and production needs all of them. It doesn't say how much work that is.

beats.trigger: The report carries the evidence and decisions.
beats.got: The output is a report with evidence and a recorded decision, and the check can be reused.

beats.trigger: Read the agent's summary and push back where it's wrong
beats.got: The agent adds rules to the standing instructions file, and I review them.

beats.trigger: A skill is not a deployed service and does not settle ownership.
beats.got: Skills can be shared with colleagues, but ownership is a separate question.

beats.trigger: Mitigations add to security controls, never replace them.
beats.got: Agent controls sit on top of existing controls and don't replace them.

beats.trigger: **Write one sentence per case: "the missing organisational check was X."**
beats.got: I write one sentence on what check was missing in two real cases. The Deloitte one is a refund over a bad report, which I want to read.

beats.trigger: What check was missing around the agent's output?
beats.got: Two public failures to read before next time.

take_homes: Keep a written risk record per agent: the risk, the one fix, what's left over, and who accepted it.
The cheapest control is a system the agent never gets access to, and that has a feature cost I'd want a figure for.
'I can't tell' is a legitimate finding. It goes to the owner (legal, IT) with the evidence, not into a guess.

monday.move: Ask my controller to list what finance data an agent would touch for the month-end variance commentary, and ask IT whether that data is approved for the tool. Then run the policy check on that one use.
monday.when: Within two weeks, before any trial
monday.stop_condition: IT says the tool is not approved for finance data, or the check returns an 'I can't tell' that legal can't settle
monday.blocker: IT hasn't approved the tool for finance data

misconception.why: The packaged check carries our judgment about what matters, so the value isn't just buying a tool. Nobody said what it costs, and I still think about this mostly as a licence.

one_line: Good on how to document and accept residual risk. No costs, no payback, and too much talk of feelings. Useful for whoever signs off, but a CFO should get it in 20 minutes.
